title: Say 'splendid'
body: On the evening of his first visit, the narrator sits beside Mrs Croft on the bench at the foot of the staircase. She announces, as if she alone knew it, that there is an American flag on the moon, and asks whether that is not splendid. When he replies only 'Yes, madame', she is not satisfied and commands him to say the word 'splendid'. The narrator is both baffled and somewhat insulted. The command reminds him of how, as a child, he learnt multiplication tables by repeating after the master, sitting cross-legged on the floor of his one-room school in Tollygunge, and of his wedding, when he repeated Sanskrit verses after the priest that he barely understood. He is soft-spoken by nature and reluctant to raise his voice to an elderly woman he has just met, but he finally says the word, and then has to repeat it at the top of his lungs so that she can hear. The reply seems to please her, for her next command is that he should go and see the room.
